In a WC trial, all auditory cues were omitted, and an approximately 3-µl water reward was presented randomly from either lickport. Trials in which the animal contacted the lickport before the reward (‘early lick’) were omitted from analyses. ITIs were randomly drawn from an exponential distribution with mean 1.5 s. There were no explicit cues during the ITI to indicate to the animal which context block it was in.\\n    22→\\n    23→For the randomized delay task (Fig. 3g,h,i), mice were first fully trained on the fixed delay DR task (delay duration of 0.9 s). The delay epoch length was then randomized; the duration for each trial was randomly selected from six possible values (0.3 s, 0.6 s, 1.2 s, 1.8 s, 2.4 s and 3.6 s). The probability of each delay duration being selected was assigned such that it resembled a probability density function of an exponential distribution with τ = 0.9 s, as in ref. 44. Animals were trained on this version of the task until they became experts (>70% accuracy and <20% early lick rate).\\n    24→\\n    25→Videography analysis\\n    26→\\n    27→High-speed video was captured (400-Hz frame rate) from two cameras (FLIR, Blackfly monochrome camera, BFS-U3-16S2M-CS). One provided a side view of the mouse, and the other provided a bottom view. We tracked the movements of specific body features using DeepLabCut (Figs. 1, 3 and 4). The tongue, jaw and nose were tracked using both cameras, whereas the paws were tracked using only the bottom view. Position and velocity of each tracked feature was calculated from each camera. The x and y position of each kinematic feature was extracted from the output of DeepLabCut. Missing values were filled in with the nearest available value for all features, except for the tongue. The velocity of each feature was then calculated as the first-order derivative of the position vector. Tongue angle and length were found using the bottom camera. Tongue angle was defined as the angle between the vector pointing from the jaw to the tip of the tongue and the vector defining the direction the mouse was facing. Tongue length was calculated as the Euclidean distance from the jaw to the tip of the tongue.\\n    28→\\n    29→Motion energy\\n    30→\\n    31→The motion energy for a given frame and pixel was defined as the absolute value of the difference between the median value of the pixel across the next five frames (12.5 ms) and the median value of the pixel across the previous five frames (12.5 ms). Motion energy for each frame was then converted to a single value by taking the 99th percentile (~700 pixels) of motion energy values across the frame. Motion energy calculated in this manner was high during overt movements over small regions of pixel space, such as during whisking, while remaining relatively low during passive respiration that corresponded to subtle motion across the animal’s body. A threshold above which an animal was classed as moving was defined on a per-session basis manually. Motion energy distributions, per session, were bimodal, showing a large peak with little variance at low motion energy values and a second, smaller peak with high variance at large values. The threshold was set as the motion energy value separating these two modes. We found that this method of setting the threshold captured both short-duration and long-duration movements. Alternative methods, such as defining a baseline period of no movement against which to compare, were less successful due to the variability in timing of the movements across trials.\\n    32→\\n    33→Photoinactivation experiments\\n    34→\\n    35→Optogenetic photoinactivation was deployed on approximately 30% of trials selected at random. A ‘masking flash’ (470-mm LEDs; LUXEON Rebel LED) controlled by an Arduino Teensy microcontroller (100-ms pulses at 10 Hz) was delivered constantly for the duration of the session to prevent mice from differentiating control and photoinactivation trials. A 488-nm laser (Coherent, OBIS 488-nm LX 150-mW laser system) was used for all photoinactivation experiments. ChR2-assisted photoinactivation (Fig. 1b,c,g and Extended Data Fig. 1b–d) was performed through a cranial window (see ‘Surgical procedures’ subsection), which replaced bone over the frontal cortex. Light was delivered either at the start of the delay epoch or at the start of the response epoch (only one epoch tested per session). A power density of 1.5 mW mm−2 was used for all photoinactivation experiments.\\n    36→\\n    37→For delay epoch photoinactivation (Fig. 1g–i and Extended Data Fig. 1b), light was delivered at the onset of the delay epoch and lasted for 0.6 s, followed by a 0.2-s linear ramp down. We targeted one of three regions per session: bilateral motor cortex (ALM and tjM1), bilateral ALM or bilateral tjM1. A scanning galvo system (Thorlabs, GPS011) was used to simultaneously target both hemispheres by scanning at 40 Hz. The beam (2-mm diameter) was centered around the following locations: ALM (AP 2.5 mm, ML 1.5 mm), tjM1 (AP 1.75 mm, ML 2.25 mm) and motor cortex (that is, ALM and tjM1; AP 2.25 mm, ML 1.85 mm). Due to their proximity, when specifically targeting ALM or tjM1, Kwik-Cast (World Precision Instruments) was applied to the surrounding regions to prevent photoinactivation of other regions. For photoinactivation at the go cue or water drop (Fig. 1b,c and Extended Data Fig. 1c,d), light was delivered to the motor cortex for 0.8 s, followed by a 0.2-s ramp down beginning at the go cue/water drop presentation.\\n    38→\\n    39→\\n    40→Electrophysiology recordings\\n    41→\\n    42→Extracellular recordings were performed in the ALM using one of two types of silicon probes: H2 probes, which have two shanks, each with 32 channels with 25-µm spacing (Cambridge Neurotech), or Neuropixels 1.0 (ref. 59), which have one shank and allow recording from 384 channels arranged in a checkerboard pattern (IMEC). For recordings with H2 probes, the 64-channel voltage signals were multiplexed using a Whisper recording system (Neural Circuits, LLC), recorded on a PXI-8133 board (National Instruments) and digitized at 14 bits. The signals were demultiplexed into 64 (for H2 probes) or 384 (for Neuropixels 1.0) voltage traces sampled at 25 kHz and stored for offline analysis.\\n    43→\\n    44→At least 6 h before recording, a small craniotomy (1–1.5-mm diameter) was made over the ALM (AP 2.5 mm, ML 1.5 mm). Then, 2–5 recordings were performed on a single craniotomy on consecutive days. After inserting the probes between 900 µm and 1,100 µm (New Scale Technologies, MPM System), brain tissue was allowed to settle for at least 5 min before starting recordings. All recordings were made using SpikeGLX (https://github.com/billkarsh/SpikeGLX, phase3a release).\\n    45→\\n    46→Behavioral analysis\\n    47→\\n    48→Behavioral data were collected using Bpod r0.5 (https://www.sanworks.io/shop/products.php?productFamily=bpod). All sessions used for behavioral analysis had at least 40 correct DR trials for each direction (left or right) and 20 correct WC trials for each direction, excluding early lick and ignore trials, which were omitted from all analyses. To assess the impact of ALM photoinactivation on movement initiation, we first calculated the percent of trials with a correct lick within 600 ms of the go cue/water drop (Fig. 1c). To find the fraction of time with the tongue visible during the photoinactivation period (Extended Data Fig. 1d), for each trial we found the number of timepoints within the 1 s after the go cue/water drop where the tongue was labeled as visible by DeepLabCut and divided that by the total number of timepoints within the photoinactivation period. This was then averaged for all control or photoinactivation trials for a given session.\\n    49→\\n    50→To assess the impact of bilateral motor cortex/ALM/tjM1 photoinactivation during the delay epoch, the average motion energy during the delay epoch was calculated separately for right and left control versus photoinactivation trials (Fig. 1h and Extended Data Fig. 1b).\\n    51→\\n    52→Electrophysiology recording analysis\\n    53→\\n    54→JRCLUST (https://github.com/JaneliaSciComp/JRCLUST, version 4.1.0) and/or Kilosort 3 (ref. 61) (https://github.com/MouseLand/Kilosort) with manual curation using Phy 2 (https://github.com/cortex-lab/phy) were used for spike sorting. A unit was considered a well-isolated single unit based on manual inspection of its inter-spike interval (ISI) histogram, separation from other units and its stationarity across the session. Units that passed manual curation but had a higher ISI violation rate were called multiunits. Recording sessions were included for analysis only if they had at least 10 units (see Extended Data Fig. 2 for a distribution of neuron counts across sessions). For the DR task, we recorded 1,651 units (483 single units) in ALM from 25 sessions using nine mice. In 12 sessions from six mice, animals performed the two-context task. In total, 522 units (214 well-isolated single units) were recorded in these sessions. Finally, for the randomized delay task, we recorded 845 units (288 well-isolated single units) in ALM from 19 sessions using four mice. For subspace alignment (Figs. 5g,n, 7d,h and 8d) and single-unit selectivity analyses (Fig. 3g and Extended Data Fig. 4c), only well-isolated single units with firing rates exceeding 1 Hz were included. All units with firing rates exceeding 1 Hz were included in all other analyses.\\n    55→\\n    56→To find choice-selective neurons, 40 trials were subsampled for both right and left correct trials, and a rank-sum test was used to compare spike counts for each unit during the sample, delay or response epochs. Selective units were those with significantly different spike counts (P < 0.05) during a given epoch. Context-selective units were defined in a two-step process to ensure that we were not conflating context selectivity with slow changes in animal engagement/motivation over each session. First, 40 trials each were subsampled for DR and WC trials, and spike counts were compared (P < 0.05, rank-sum test) during the ITI (the 300 ms preceding the sample tone onset) when the animal received no external cues to indicate which context it was in. Because sessions always began with a DR block and often ended with a WC block, it is possible that differences in firing rates across contexts defined in this way could be representing time within the session. To account for this, for each unit identified in the first step, we calculated the difference in spike rate for each pair of DR and WC blocks (for example, a session with five blocks, DR–WC–DR–WC–DR, would have nPairs = 4 adjacent, overlapping block pairs) and included units as context selective only if their preferred context (context with a higher spike rate) was the same for at least nPairs − 1 of the block pairs.\\n    57→\\n    58→Selectivity in the neural population (Extended Data Fig. 4c) was calculated as the difference in spike rate on preferred − non-preferred trials in choice-selective units, with preferred trials referring to the trial type with a higher spike rate for each unit.\\n    59→\"\n532:            \"content\": \"1→# Code accompanying Hasnain, Birnbaum et dict = {}, **kwargs):\\n   694→    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n   695→    Trains a common decoder for all sessions to predict output from neural and input data.\\n   696→    Jointly learns projection matrices for each session and separate shared decoders for each output dimension.\\n   697→\\n   698→    Inputs:\\n   699→        neural: neural activity. neural is a list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list\\n   700→                of length ntrials[session], and neural[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (nneurons[session], T[session][trial]),\\n   701→                dtype = float32, giving the neural activity for that trial\\n   702→        input: variables beyond neural activity the decoder should input, e.g. the stimulis, condition. input is a list of\\n   703→                length nsessions, input[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and input[session][trial] is a numpy array of\\n   704→                shape (dinput, T[session][trial]), dtype = float32. with the input variable(s) for each timepoint.\\n   705→                dinput is the number of inputs. For discrete inputs, use a one-hot encoding.\\n   706→        output: variables we want to decode. output is a list of length nsessions, output[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],\\n   707→                and output[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]) of dtype = int with\\n   708→                categorical values for each timepoint. Each output[idx, t] is an integer from 0 to ncategories[idx]-1.\\n   709→        metadata: optional dict with additional information about the experiment.\\n   710→\\n   711→        Algorithm hyperparameters can be passed as keyword arguments:\\n   712→        npcs: number of projected dimensions to use (default: 10)\\n   713→        num_epochs: number of training epochs (default: 200)\\n   714→        lr: learning rate (default: 0.001)\\n   715→        l1_weight: L1 regularization weight for projection matrices (default: 1e-4)\\n   716→        svd_max_samples: maximum number of timepoints to use for SVD initialization (default: 50000).\\n   717→                         If a session has more timepoints than this, a random subset will be used.\\n   718→        svd_max_neurons: maximum number of neurons to use for SVD initialization (default: 2000).\\n   719→                         If a session has more neurons than this, random Gaussian projection will be used.\\n   720→                         The final weight is the product of the random projection and SVD matrices.\\n   721→        ncategories: optional list of length doutput giving number of categories for each output dimension.\\n   722→                     If not provided, will be inferred from data.\\n   723→        balanced_loss: if True, use class-weighted cross-entropy loss to compensate for class imbalance.\\n   724→                       Weights are inverse of class frequency. Default: False.\\n   725→\\n   726→    Returns:\\n   727→        model: dict with trained decoder parameters. dict with the keys:\\n   728→            'projection': list of length nsessions, projection[session] is a torch tensor of shape (npcs, nneurons[session])\\n   729→            'decoder': list of length doutput, decoder[out_dim] is a torch linear layer for that output dimension\\n   730→            'ncategories': list of length doutput, ncategories[out_dim] is the number of categories for that output\\n   731→            'device': torch device used for training\\n   732→\\n   733→    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n   734→\\n   735→    model = {\\n   736→        'projection': [],\\n   737→        'decoder': [],\\n   738→        'ncategories': [],\\n   739→        'device': None\\n   740→    }\\n   741→\\n   742→    npcs = kwargs.get('npcs', 10)\\n   743→    num_epochs = kwargs.get('num_epochs', 200)\\n   744→    lr = kwargs.get('lr', 0.001)\\n   745→    l1_weight = kwargs.get('l1_weight', 1e-4)\\n   746→    device_str = kwargs.get('device', None)\\n   747→    balanced_loss = kwargs.get('balanced_loss', False)\\n   748→\\n   749→    nsessions = len(neural)\\n   750→    if device_str is not None:\\n   751→        device = torch.device(device_str)\\n   752→    else:\\n   753→        device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')\\n   754→\\n   755→    model['device'] = device\\n   756→    print('Using device:', device)\\n   757→\\n   758→    # Prepare training data using helper function\\n   759→    session_data, dinput, doutput = _prepare_session_data(neural, input, output, device)\\n   760→\\n   761→    # Determine number of categories for each output dimension\\n   762→    if 'ncategories' in kwargs:\\n   763→        ncategories = kwargs['ncategories']\\n   764→    else:\\n   765→        ncategories = []\\n   766→        for out_dim in range(doutput):\\n   767→            max_cat = 0\\n   768→            for session in range(nsessions):\\n   769→                if session_data[session] is None:\\n   770→                    continue\\n   771→                max_cat = max(max_cat, int(session_data[session]['output'][:, out_dim].max().item()))\\n   772→            ncategories.append(max_cat + 1)\\n   773→\\n   774→    model['ncategories'] = ncategories\\n   775→\\n   776→    # Compute class weights (always, for use in chance computation and optionally for balanced loss)\\n   777→    class_weights = []\\n   778→    class_fractions = []  # Store fractions for chance computation\\n   779→    for out_dim in range(doutput):\\n   780→        # Count occurrences of each class across all sessions\\n   781→        class_counts = np.zeros(ncategories[out_dim])\\n   782→        for session in range(nsessions):\\n   783→            if session_data[session] is None:\\n   784→                continue\\n   785→            outputs = session_data[session]['output'][:, out_dim].cpu().numpy()\\n   786→            for c in range(ncategories[out_dim]):\\n   787→                class_counts[c] += np.sum(outputs == c)\\n   788→        # Store class fractions for chance computation\\n   789→        total = np.sum(class_counts)\\n   790→        fractions = class_counts / total\\n   791→        class_fractions.append(fractions)\\n   792→        # Compute weights as inverse of frequency (with smoothing to avoid division by zero)\\n   793→        weights = total / (ncategories[out_dim] * np.maximum(class_counts, 1))\\n   794→        # Normalize weights to sum to 1 (so each output dimension is equally weighted)\\n   795→        weights = weights / np.sum(weights)\\n   796→        class_weights.append(torch.tensor(weights, dtype=torch.float32, device=device))\\n   797→\\n   798→    model['class_weights'] = class_weights\\n   799→    model['class_fractions'] = class_fractions\\n   800→\\n   801→    if balanced_loss:\\n   802→        print(f\\\"Using balanced loss with class weights:\\\")\\n   803→        for out_dim in range(doutput):\\n   804→            print(f\\\"  Output {out_dim}: {class_weights[out_dim].cpu().numpy()}\\\")\\n   805→\\n   806→    # Initialize projection matrices for each session\\n   807→    svd_max_samples = kwargs.get('svd_max_samples', 50000)  # Max timepoints to use for SVD initialization\\n   808→    svd_max_neurons = kwargs.get('svd_max_neurons', 2000)   # Max neurons to use for SVD initialization\\n   809→    projection_layers = []\\n   810→    for session in range(nsessions):\\n   811→        nneurons = session_data[session]['nneurons']\\n   812→        proj = nn.Linear(nneurons, npcs, bias=False).to(device)\\n   813→\\n   814→        # Initialize with SVD for stability (use V from SVD of neural data)\\n   815→        # For neural data with shape (n_timepoints, n_neurons), SVD gives principal components in V\\n   816→        # Use random subsets if data is too large\\n   817→        n_timepoints = session_data[session]['neural'].shape[0]\\n   818→\\n   819→        # Sample timepoints if needed\\n   820→        if n_timepoints > svd_max_samples:\\n   821→            time_indices = torch.randperm(n_timepoints)[:svd_max_samples]\\n   822→            neural_subset = session_data[session]['neural'][time_indices, :]\\n   823→            print(f\\\"Session {session}: Using {svd_max_samples} of {n_timepoints} timepoints for SVD initialization\\\")\\n   824→        else:\\n   825→            neural_subset = session_data[session]['neural']\\n   826→\\n   827→        # Use random projection if too many neurons\\n   828→        if nneurons > svd_max_neurons:\\n   829→            # Create random Gaussian projection matrix: (n_neurons, svd_max_neurons)\\n   830→            P = torch.randn(nneurons, svd_max_neurons)\\n   831→            # Project neural data: (n_timepoints, n_neurons) @ (n_neurons, svd_max_neurons) = (n_timepoints, svd_max_neurons)\\n   832→            neural_projected = neural_subset @ P\\n   833→            print(f\\\"Session {session}: Using random projection to {svd_max_neurons} of {nneurons} neurons for SVD initialization\\\")\\n   834→\\n   835→            # SVD on projected data\\n   836→            _, _, V = torch.svd(neural_projected, some=True)\\n   837→            # V has shape (svd_max_neurons, min(n_timepoints_subset, svd_max_neurons))\\n   838→\\n   839→            # Compose: final weight = (P @ V[:, :npcs]).T = V[:, :npcs].T @ P.T\\n   840→            n_components = min(npcs, V.shape[1])\\n   841→            proj.weight.data[:n_components, :] = (V[:, :n_components].T @ P.T).to(device).clone()\\n   842→        else:\\n   843→            # Standard SVD without random projection\\n   844→            _, _, V = torch.svd(neural_subset, some=True)\\n   845→            # V has shape (n_neurons, min(n_timepoints_subset, n_neurons))\\n   846→            n_components = min(npcs, V.shape[1])\\n   847→            proj.weight.data[:n_components, :] = V[:, :n_components].T.to(device).clone()\\n   848→\\n   849→        # Initialize remaining components randomly if needed\\n   850→        if n_components < npcs:\\n   851→            nn.init.orthogonal_(proj.weight.data[n_components:, :])\\n   852→\\n   853→        projection_layers.append(proj)\\n   854→\\n   855→    # Initialize separate decoders for each output dimension\\n   856→    decoders = []\\n   857→    for out_dim in range(doutput):\\n   858→        decoder = nn.Linear(npcs + dinput, ncategories[out_dim]).to(device)\\n   859→        decoders.append(decoder)\\n   860→\\n   861→    # Collect all parameters\\n   862→    all_params = []\\n   863→    for proj in projection_layers:\\n   864→        all_params.extend(proj.parameters())\\n   865→    for decoder in decoders:\\n   866→        all_params.extend(decoder.parameters())\\n   867→\\n   868→    optimizer = optim.Adam(all_params, lr=lr)\\n   869→\\n   870→    # Loss function with reduction='none' for manual weighting (matches torch_brain)\\n   871→    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction='none')\\n   872→\\n   873→    # Training loop\\n   874→    # Data stays on CPU; each session is moved to GPU one at a time.\\n   875→    # backward() is called per session to free the computation graph before\\n   876→    # loading the next session. Gradients accumulate across sessions.\\n   877→    for epoch in range(num_epochs):\\n   878→        epoch_loss = 0.\\n   879→        optimizer.zero_grad()\\n   880→\\n   881→        for session in range(nsessions):\\n   882→            if session_data[session] is None:\\n   883→                continue\\n   884→            # Move this session's data to device\\n   885→            neural_batch = session_data[session]['neural'].to(device)\\n   886→            input_batch = session_data[session]['input'].to(device)\\n   887→            output_batch = session_data[session]['output'].to(device)\\n   888→\\n   889→            # Forward pass - shared projection\\n   890→            projected = projection_layers[session](neural_batch)\\n   891→            combined = torch.cat([projected, input_batch], dim=1)\\n   892→\\n   893→            # Compute loss for each output dimension\\n   894→            session_loss = torch.tensor(0., device=device)\\n   895→            for out_dim in range(doutput):\\n   896→                logits = decoders[out_dim](combined)\\n   897→                target = output_batch[:, out_dim]\\n   898→                loss_per_sample = criterion(logits, target)\\n   899→\\n   900→                if balanced_loss:\\n   901→                    # Manual per-sample weighting (matches torch_brain exactly)\\n   902→                    sample_weights = class_weights[out_dim][target]\\n   903→                    session_loss += (sample_weights * loss_per_sample).sum() / sample_weights.sum()\\n   904→                else:\\n   905→                    session_loss += loss_per_sample.mean()\\n   906→\\n   907→            # Add L1 regularization on current session's projection matrix\\n   908→            if l1_weight > 0:\\n   909→                l1_loss = torch.sum(torch.abs(projection_layers[session].weight))\\n   910→                session_loss += l1_weight * l1_loss\\n   911→\\n   912→            # Backward per session: frees computation graph, accumulates gradients\\n   913→            session_loss.backward()\\n   914→            epoch_loss += session_loss.item()\\n   915→\\n   916→        optimizer.step()\\n   917→\\n   918→        if ((epoch + 1) % 10 == 0) or (epoch < 10):\\n   919→            # Loss is sum of per-output-dim means across sessions\\n   920→            # Normalize by (nsessions * doutput) to get average per output per session\\n   921→            train_loss_normalized = epoch_loss / (nsessions * doutput)\\n   922→            print(f'Epoch [{epoch+1}/{num_epochs}], Loss: {train_loss_normalized:.6f}')\\n   923→\\n   924→    # Store trained parameters\\n   925→    for session in range(nsessions):\\n   926→        model['projection'].append(projection_layers[session].weight.data.clone())\\n   927→    model['decoder'] = decoders\\n   928→\\n   929→    return model\\n   930→\\n   931→def predict(neural: list, input: list, model: dict, sessionid: list | None = None, metadata: dict = {}):\\n   932→    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n   933→    Uses a trained decoder model to predict output from neural and input data.\\n   934→\\n   935→    Inputs:\\n   936→        neural: neural activity. neural is a list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list\\n   937→                of length ntrials[session], and neural[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (nneurons[session], T[session][trial]),\\n   938→                dtype = float32, giving the neural activity for that trial\\n   939→        input: variables beyond neural activity the decoder should input, e.g. the stimulis, condition. input is a list of\\n   940→                length nsessions, input[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and input[session][trial] is a numpy array of\\n   941→                shape (dinput, T[session][trial]), dtype = float32. with the input variable(s) for each timepoint.\\n   942→                dinput is the number of inputs. print(s)\\\\n\\\\n    # build summary dict\\\\n    summary = {\\\\n        'nsessions': nsessions,\\\\n        'ntrials_total': sum(ntrials_per_session),\\\\n        'dinput': dinput,\\\\n        'doutput': doutput,\\\\n        'T_mean': float(np.mean(mean_T)),\\\\n        'T_median': float(np.median(mean_T)),\\\\n        'T_min': int(np.min(min_T)),\\\\n        'T_max':   if 'subjects' in data:\\\\n        summary['nsubjects'] = len(data['subjects'])\\\\n        summary['subjects'] = data['subjects']\\\\n    if 'subject_idx' in data:\\\\n        unique, counts = return fig, ax\\\\n\\\\ndef random_sample_trials(data, nsample, trial_indices=None):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    Randomly sample trials across all sessions\\\\n    Inputs:\\\\n        data: dict with keys 'neural', 'input', 'output' as described in train_decoder.py\\\\n        nsample: number of trials to sample\\\\n        trial_indices: optional list of length nsessions, trial_indices[session] is a numpy array\\\\n                       with valid trial indices for that session (e.g., test_indices from validate_decoder).\\\\n                       If None, samples from all trials.\\\\n    Returns:\\\\n        sessionplot: numpy array of shape (nsample,), session indices for sampled trials\\\\n        trialplot: numpy array of shape (nsample,), trial indices for sampled trials\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n    nsessions = len(data['neural'])\\\\n\\\\n    if trial_indices is None:\\\\n        # Sample from all trials\\\\n        ntrials_per_session = [len(data['neural'][i]) for i in range(nsessions)]\\\\n        valid_trials_per_session = [np.arange(n) for n in ntrials_per_session]\\\\n    else:\\\\n        # Sample only from specified trial indices\\\\n        ntrials_per_session = [len(trial_indices[i]) for i in range(nsessions)]\\\\n        valid_trials_per_session = trial_indices\\\\n\\\\n    # Sample sessions with equal probability\\\\n    sessionplot = np.random.choice(nsessions, nsample, replace=nsample > nsessions)\\\\n\\\\n    trialplot = np.full((nsample,), -1, dtype=int)\\\\n    for session in range(nsessions):\\\\n        idx = session == sessionplot\\\\n        ncurr = np.count_nonzero(idx)\\\\n        if ncurr == 0:\\\\n            continue\\\\n        valid_trials = valid_trials_per_session[session]\\\\n        if len(valid_trials) == 0:\\\\n            continue\\\\n        # Sample from valid trials and map back to original trial indices\\\\n        sampled = np.random.choice(len(valid_trials), ncurr, replace=len(valid_trials) < ncurr)\\\\n        trialplot[idx] = valid_trials[sampled]\\\\n\\\\n    return sessionplot, trialplot\\\\n    \\\\n\\\\ndef _prepare_session_data(neural: list, input: list, output: list, device, doutput: int = None):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    Helper function to prepare session data for training/validation.\\\\n\\\\n    Inputs:\\\\n        neural: list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list of trials\\\\n        input: list of length nsessions, input[session] is a list of trials\\\\n        output: list of length nsessions, output[session] is a list of trials\\\\n        device: torch device to move data to\\\\n        doutput: number of output dimensions (if None, inferred from data)\\\\n\\\\n    Returns:\\\\n        session_data: list of dicts with 'neural', 'input', 'output', 'nneurons' tensors\\\\n        dinput: input dimension\\\\n        doutput: output dimension\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    nsessions = len(neural)\\\\n\\\\n    # Determine dimensions\\\\n    # Find first non-empty session/trial\\\\n    for sess in range(nsessions):\\\\n        if len(neural[sess]) > 0:\\\\n            if input[sess][0].ndim == 1:\\\\n                dinput = len(input[sess][0])\\\\n            else:\\\\n                dinput = input[sess][0].shape[0]\\\\n            if doutput is None:\\\\n                if output[sess][0].ndim == 1:\\\\n                    doutput = len(output[sess][0])\\\\n                else:\\\\n                    doutput = output[sess][0].shape[0]\\\\n            break\\\\n\\\\n    # Process input/output: replicate 1D along time axis\\\\n    input_processed = []\\\\n    output_processed = []\\\\n    for session in range(nsessions):\\\\n        input_session = []\\\\n        output_session = []\\\\n        for trial in range(len(neural[session])):\\\\n            T = neural[session][trial].shape[1]\\\\n            if input[session][trial].ndim == 1:\\\\n                input_trial = np.tile(input[session][trial][:, np.newaxis], (1, T))\\\\n            else:\\\\n                input_trial = input[session][trial]\\\\n            input_session.append(input_trial)\\\\n            if output[session][trial].ndim == 1:\\\\n                output_trial = np.tile(output[session][trial][:, np.newaxis], (1, T))\\\\n            else:\\\\n                output_trial = output[session][trial]\\\\n            output_session.append(output_trial)\\\\n        input_processed.append(input_session)\\\\n        output_processed.append(output_session)\\\\n\\\\n    # Create session data tensors\\\\n    session_data = []\\\\n    for session in range(nsessions):\\\\n        if len(neural[session]) == 0:\\\\n            session_data.append(None)\\\\n            continue\\\\n        neural_concat = np.concatenate([neural[session][trial].T.astype(np.float32) for trial in range(len(neural[session]))], axis=0)\\\\n        input_concat = np.concatenate([input_processed[session][trial].T for trial in range(len(input_processed[session]))], axis=0).astype(np.float32)\\\\n        output_concat = np.concatenate([output_processed[session][trial].T for trial in range(len(output_processed[session]))], axis=0).astype(np.int64)\\\\n        session_data.append({\\\\n            'neural': torch.from_numpy(neural_concat),\\\\n            'input': torch.from_numpy(input_concat),\\\\n            'output': torch.from_numpy(output_concat),\\\\n            'nneurons': neural_concat.shape[1]\\\\n        })\\\\n\\\\n    return session_data, dinput, doutput\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef train_decoder(neural: list, input: list, output: list, metadata: dict = {}, **kwargs):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    Trains a common decoder for all sessions to predict output from neural and input data.\\\\n    Jointly learns projection matrices for each session and separate shared decoders for each output dimension.\\\\n\\\\n    Inputs:\\\\n        neural: neural activity. neural is a list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list\\\\n                of length ntrials[session], and neural[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (nneurons[session], T[session][trial]),\\\\n                dtype = float32, giving the neural activity for that trial\\\\n        input: variables beyond neural activity the decoder should input, e.g. the stimulis, condition. input is a list of\\\\n                length nsessions, input[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and input[session][trial] is a numpy array of\\\\n                shape (dinput, T[session][trial]), dtype = float32. with the input variable(s) for each timepoint.\\\\n                dinput is the number of inputs. For discrete inputs, use a one-hot encoding.\\\\n        output: variables we want to decode. output is a list of length nsessions, output[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],\\\\n                and output[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]) of dtype = int with\\\\n                categorical values for each timepoint. Each output[idx, t] is an integer from 0 to ncategories[idx]-1.\\\\n        metadata: optional dict with additional information about the experiment.\\\\n\\\\n        Algorithm hyperparameters can be passed as keyword arguments:\\\\n        npcs: number of projected dimensions to use (default: 10)\\\\n        num_epochs: number of training epochs (default: 200)\\\\n        lr: learning rate (default: 0.001)\\\\n        l1_weight: L1 regularization weight for projection matrices (default: 1e-4)\\\\n        svd_max_samples: maximum number of timepoints to use for SVD initialization (default: 50000).\\\\n                         If a session has more timepoints than this, a random subset will be used.\\\\n        svd_max_neurons: maximum number of neurons to use for SVD initialization (default: 2000).\\\\n                         If a session has more neurons than this, random Gaussian projection will be used.\\\\n                         The final weight is the product of the random projection and SVD matrices.\\\\n        ncategories: optional list of length doutput giving number of categories for each output dimension.\\\\n                     If not provided, will be inferred from data.\\\\n        balanced_loss: if True, use class-weighted cross-entropy loss to compensate for class imbalance.\\\\n                       Weights are inverse of class frequency. Default: False.\\\\n\\\\n    Returns:\\\\n        model: dict with trained decoder parameters. dict with the keys:\\\\n            'projection': list of length nsessions, projection[session] is a torch tensor of shape (npcs, nneurons[session])\\\\n            'decoder': list of length doutput, decoder[out_dim] is a torch linear layer for that output dimension\\\\n            'ncategories': list of length doutput, ncategories[out_dim] is the number of categories for that output\\\\n            'device': torch device used for training\\\\n\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n    model = {\\\\n        'projection': [],\\\\n        'decoder': [],\\\\n        'ncategories': [],\\\\n        'device': None\\\\n    }\\\\n\\\\n    npcs = kwargs.get('npcs', 10)\\\\n    num_epochs = kwargs.get('num_epochs', 200)\\\\n    lr = kwargs.get('lr', 0.001)\\\\n    l1_weight = kwargs.get('l1_weight', 1e-4)\\\\n    device_str = kwargs.get('device', None)\\\\n    balanced_loss = kwargs.get('balanced_loss', False)\\\\n\\\\n    nsessions = len(neural)\\\\n    if device_str is not None:\\\\n        device = torch.device(device_str)\\\\n    else:\\\\n        device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')\\\\n\\\\n    model['device'] = device\\\\n    print('Using device:', device)\\\\n\\\\n    # Prepare training data using helper function\\\\n    session_data, dinput, doutput = _prepare_session_data(neural, input, output, device)\\\\n\\\\n    # Determine number of categories for each output dimension\\\\n    if 'ncategories' in kwargs:\\\\n        ncategories = kwargs['ncategories']\\\\n    else:\\\\n        ncategories = []\\\\n        for out_dim in range(doutput):\\\\n            max_cat = 0\\\\n            for session in range(nsessions):\\\\n                if session_data[session] is None:\\\\n                    continue\\\\n                max_cat = max(max_cat, int(session_data[session]['output'][:, out_dim].max().item()))\\\\n            ncategories.append(max_cat + 1)\\\\n\\\\n    model['ncategories'] = ncategories\\\\n\\\\n    # Compute class weights (always, for use in chance computation and optionally for balanced loss)\\\\n    class_weights = []\\\\n    class_fractions = []  # Store fractions for chance computation\\\\n    for out_dim in range(doutput):\\\\n        # Count occurrences of each class across all sessions\\\\n        class_counts = np.zeros(ncategories[out_dim])\\\\n        for session in range(nsessions):\\\\n            if session_data[session] is None:\\\\n                continue\\\\n            outputs = session_data[session]['output'][:, out_dim].cpu().numpy()\\\\n            for c in range(ncategories[out_dim]):\\\\n                class_counts[c] += np.sum(outputs == c)\\\\n        # Store class fractions for chance computation\\\\n        total = np.sum(class_counts)\\\\n        fractions = class_counts / total\\\\n        class_fractions.append(fractions)\\\\n        # Compute weights as inverse of frequency (with smoothing to avoid division by zero)\\\\n        weights = total / (ncategories[out_dim] * np.maximum(class_counts, 1))\\\\n        # Normalize weights to sum to 1 (so each output dimension is equally weighted)\\\\n        weights = weights / np.sum(weights)\\\\n        class_weights.append(torch.tensor(weights, dtype=torch.float32, device=device))\\\\n\\\\n    model['class_weights'] = class_weights\\\\n    model['class_fractions'] = class_fractions\\\\n\\\\n    if balanced_loss:\\\\n        print(f\\\\\\\"Using balanced loss with class weights:\\\\\\\")\\\\n        for out_dim in range(doutput):\\\\n            print(f\\\\\\\"  Output {out_dim}: {class_weights[out_dim].cpu().numpy()}\\\\\\\")\\\\n\\\\n    # Initialize projection matrices for each session\\\\n    svd_max_samples = kwargs.get('svd_max_samples', 50000)  # Max timepoints to use for SVD initialization\\\\n    svd_max_neurons = kwargs.get('svd_max_neurons', 2000)   # Max neurons to use for SVD initialization\\\\n    projection_layers = []\\\\n    for session in range(nsessions):\\\\n        nneurons = session_data[session]['nneurons']\\\\n        proj = nn.Linear(nneurons, npcs, bias=False).to(device)\\\\n\\\\n        # Initialize with SVD for stability (use V from SVD of neural data)\\\\n        # For neural data with shape (n_timepoints, n_neurons), SVD gives principal components in V\\\\n        # Use random subsets if data is too large\\\\n        n_timepoints = session_data[session]['neural'].shape[0]\\\\n\\\\n        # Sample timepoints if needed\\\\n        if n_timepoints > svd_max_samples:\\\\n            time_indices = torch.randperm(n_timepoints)[:svd_max_samples]\\\\n            neural_subset = session_data[session]['neural'][time_indices, :]\\\\n            print(f\\\\\\\"Session {session}: Using {svd_max_samples} of {n_timepoints} timepoints for SVD initialization\\\\\\\")\\\\n        else:\\\\n            neural_subset = session_data[session]['neural']\\\\n\\\\n        # Use random projection if too many neurons\\\\n        if nneurons > svd_max_neurons:\\\\n            # Create random Gaussian projection matrix: (n_neurons, svd_max_neurons)\\\\n            P = torch.randn(nneurons, svd_max_neurons)\\\\n            # Project neural data: (n_timepoints, n_neurons) @ (n_neurons, svd_max_neurons) = (n_timepoints, svd_max_neurons)\\\\n            neural_projected = neural_subset @ P\\\\n            print(f\\\\\\\"Session {session}: Using random projection to {svd_max_neurons} of {nneurons} neurons for SVD initialization\\\\\\\")\\\\n\\\\n            # SVD on projected data\\\\n            _, _, V = torch.svd(neural_projected, some=True)\\\\n            # V has shape (svd_max_neurons, min(n_timepoints_subset, svd_max_neurons))\\\\n\\\\n            # Compose: final weight = (P @ V[:, :npcs]).T = V[:, :npcs].T @ P.T\\\\n            n_components = min(npcs, V.shape[1])\\\\n            proj.weight.data[:n_components, :] = (V[:, :n_components].T @ P.T).to(device).clone()\\\\n        else:\\\\n            # Standard SVD without random projection\\\\n            _, _, V = torch.svd(neural_subset, some=True)\\\\n            # V has shape (n_neurons, min(n_timepoints_subset, n_neurons))\\\\n            n_components = min(npcs, V.shape[1])\\\\n            proj.weight.data[:n_components, :] = V[:, :n_components].T.to(device).clone()\\\\n\\\\n        # Initialize remaining components randomly if needed\\\\n        if n_components < npcs:\\\\n            nn.init.orthogonal_(proj.weight.data[n_components:, :])\\\\n\\\\n        projection_layers.append(proj)\\\\n\\\\n    # Initialize separate decoders for each output dimension\\\\n    decoders = []\\\\n    for out_dim in range(doutput):\\\\n        decoder = nn.Linear(npcs + dinput, ncategories[out_dim]).to(device)\\\\n        decoders.append(decoder)\\\\n\\\\n    # Collect all parameters\\\\n    all_params = []\\\\n    for proj in projection_layers:\\\\n        all_params.extend(proj.parameters())\\\\n    for decoder in decoders:\\\\n        all_params.extend(decoder.parameters())\\\\n\\\\n    optimizer = optim.Adam(all_params, lr=lr)\\\\n\\\\n    # Loss function with reduction='none' for manual weighting (matches torch_brain)\\\\n    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction='none')\\\\n\\\\n    # Training loop\\\\n    # Data stays on CPU; each session is moved to GPU one at a time.\\\\n    # backward() is called per session to free the computation graph before\\\\n    # loading the next session. Gradients accumulate across sessions.\\\\n    for epoch in range(num_epochs):\\\\n        epoch_loss = 0.\\\\n        optimizer.zero_grad()\\\\n\\\\n        for session in range(nsessions):\\\\n            if session_data[session] is None:\\\\n                continue\\\\n            # Move this session's data to device\\\\n            neural_batch = session_data[session]['neural'].to(device)\\\\n            input_batch = session_data[session]['input'].to(device)\\\\n            output_batch = session_data[session]['output'].to(device)\\\\n\\\\n            # Forward pass - shared projection\\\\n            projected = projection_layers[session](neural_batch)\\\\n            combined = torch.cat([projected, input_batch], dim=1)\\\\n\\\\n            # Compute loss for each output dimension\\\\n            session_loss = torch.tensor(0., device=device)\\\\n            for out_dim in range(doutput):\\\\n                logits = decoders[out_dim](combined)\\\\n                target = output_batch[:, out_dim]\\\\n                loss_per_sample = criterion(logits, target)\\\\n\\\\n                if balanced_loss:\\\\n                    # Manual per-sample weighting (matches torch_brain exactly)\\\\n                    sample_weights = class_weights[out_dim][target]\\\\n                    session_loss += (sample_weights * loss_per_sample).sum() / sample_weights.sum()\\\\n                else:\\\\n                    session_loss += loss_per_sample.mean()\\\\n\\\\n            # Add L1 regularization on current session's projection matrix\\\\n            if l1_weight > 0:\\\\n                l1_loss = torch.sum(torch.abs(projection_layers[session].weight))\\\\n                session_loss += l1_weight * l1_loss\\\\n\\\\n            # Backward per session: frees computation graph, accumulates gradients\\\\n            session_loss.backward()\\\\n            epoch_loss += session_loss.item()\\\\n\\\\n        optimizer.step()\\\\n\\\\n        if ((epoch + 1) % 10 == 0) or (epoch < 10):\\\\n            # Loss is sum of per-output-dim means across sessions\\\\n            # Normalize by (nsessions * doutput) to get average per output per session\\\\n            train_loss_normalized = epoch_loss / (nsessions * doutput)\\\\n            print(f'Epoch [{epoch+1}/{num_epochs}], Loss: {train_loss_normalized:.6f}')\\\\n\\\\n    # Store trained parameters\\\\n    for session in range(nsessions):\\\\n        model['projection'].append(projection_layers[session].weight.data.clone())\\\\n    model['decoder'] = decoders\\\\n\\\\n    return model\\\\n\\\\ndef predict(neural: list, input: list, model: dict, sessionid: list | None = None, metadata: dict = {}):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    Uses a trained decoder model to predict output from neural and input data.\\\\n\\\\n    Inputs:\\\\n        neural: neural activity. neural is a list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list\\\\n                of length ntrials[session], and neural[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (nneurons[session], T[session][trial]),\\\\n                dtype = float32, giving the neural activity for that trial\\\\n        input: variables beyond neural activity the decoder should input, e.g. the stimulis, condition. input is a list of\\\\n                length nsessions, input[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and input[session][trial] is a numpy array of\\\\n                shape (dinput, T[session][trial]), dtype = float32. with the input variable(s) for each timepoint.\\\\n                dinput is the number of inputs. For discrete inputs, use a one-hot encoding.\\\\n        model: dict with trained decoder parameters. dict with the keys:\\\\n                'projection': list of length nsessions, projection[session] is a torch tensor\\\\n                'decoder': list of length doutput, decoder[out_dim] is a torch linear layer for that output dimension\\\\n                'ncategories': list session_pcs = []\\\\n            projection = model['projection'][session]\\\\n\\\\n            for trial in range(ntrials):\\\\n                # Get trial data\\\\n                neural_trial = torch.from_numpy(neural[sessionidx][trial].T.astype(np.float32)).to(device)  # (T, nneurons)\\\\n                input_trial = input: list, output: list, metadata: str | None = None,\\\\n                           nsets: int = 5,\\\\n                           eval_fn=None,\\\\n                           **kwargs):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    Cross-validates the decoder function. Performs nsets-fold cross-validation, training the decoder on nsets-1 sets and testing on\\\\n    the held-out set. Each cross-validation set contains 1/nsets of the trials from each session.\\\\n    Finds a random split of trials for each session into nsets sets, then, for each set, trains the decoder on the other nsets-1 sets and\\\\n    computes the predictions on the held out set.\\\\n    Then computes evaluation metric (F1 score or accuracy) for each output dimension\\\\n    Inputs:\\\\n        neural: neural activity. neural is a list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list\\\\n                of length ntrials[session], and neural[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (nneurons[session], T[session][trial]),\\\\n                dtype = float32, giving the neural activity for that trial\\\\n        input: variables beyond neural activity the decoder should input, e.g. the stimulis, condition. input is a list of\\\\n                length nsessions, input[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and input[session][trial] is a numpy array of\\\\n                shape (dinput, T[session][trial]), dtype = float32. with the input variable(s) for each timepoint.\\\\n                dinput is the number of inputs. For discrete inputs, use a one-hot encoding.\\\\n        output: the ground truth output for each trial. output is a list of length nsessions, output[session] is a list of\\\\n                length ntrials[session], and output[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]),\\\\n                dtype = float32 or int. with the output variable(s) for each timepoint.\\\\n        metadata: optional dict with additional information about the experiment.\\\\n        train_decoder: function to train the decoder. Should have the signature\\\\n                model = train_decoder(neural_train, input_train, output_train, metadata, **kwargs)\\\\n                Default: train_decoder_linear\\\\n        predict: function to predict using the trained decoder. Should have the signature\\\\n                predictions = predict(neural_test, input_test, model, sessionid, metadata)\\\\n                Default: predict_linear\\\\n        nsets: number of cross-validation sets (default: 5)\\\\n        eval_fn: evaluation function to compute performance metric. Should have the signature\\\\n                scores = eval_fn(predictions, output)\\\\n                Default: accuracy_all_sessions (for binary outputs), can use accuracy_all_sessions for categorical\\\\n    kwargs are passed to train_decoder\\\\n    Returns:\\\\n        scores: numpy array of shape (doutput,) with the evaluation metric for each output dimension\\\\n        predictions: list of length nsessions, predictions[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],\\\\n                and predictions[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial])\\\\n                with the predicted output variable(s) for each timepoint.\\\\n        pcs: list of length nsessions, pcs[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],\\\\n                and pcs[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (npcs, T[session][trial]) with the projected neural data.\\\\n        confidences: list of length nsessions, confidences[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],\\\\n                and confidences[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]) with the confidence scores.\\\\n        trial_splits: list of length nsessions, trial_splits[session] is a list of length nsets,\\\\n                trial_splits[session][set] is a numpy array with the trial indices for that set for that session.\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n    if eval_fn is None:\\\\n        eval_fn = accuracy_all_sessions\\\\n\\\\n    nsessions = len(neural)\\\\n\\\\n    # Create random splits of trials for each session\\\\n    trial_splits = []\\\\n    for session in range(nsessions):\\\\n        ntrials = len(neural[session])\\\\n        trial_indices = np.random.permutation(ntrials)\\\\n\\\\n        # Split trial indices into nsets\\\\n        split_indices = np.array_split(trial_indices, nsets)\\\\n        trial_splits.append(split_indices)\\\\n\\\\n    # Initialize storage for all predictions (will be filled in during cross-validation)\\\\n    all_predictions = [[None for _ in range(len(neural[session]))] for session in range(nsessions)]\\\\n    all_pcs = [[None for _ in range(len(neural[session]))] for session in range(nsessions)]\\\\n    all_confidences = [[None for _ in range(len(neural[session]))] for session in range(nsessions)]\\\\n\\\\n    # Perform cross-validation\\\\n    for test_set in tqdm.trange(nsets):\\\\n        # Create training and test data for this fold\\\\n        train_neural = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]\\\\n        train_input = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]\\\\n        train_output = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]\\\\n\\\\n        test_neural = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]\\\\n        test_input = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]\\\\n        test_output = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]\\\\n\\\\n        test_trial_indices = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]\\\\n\\\\n        for session in range(nsessions):\\\\n            for set_idx in range(nsets):\\\\n                trials_in_set = trial_splits[session][set_idx]\\\\n\\\\n                if set_idx == test_set:\\\\n                    # These trials go to test set\\\\n                    for trial_idx in trials_in_set:\\\\n                        test_neural[session].append(neural[session][trial_idx])\\\\n                        test_input[session].append(input[session][trial_idx])\\\\n                        test_output[session].append(output[session][trial_idx])\\\\n                        test_trial_indices[session].append(trial_idx)\\\\n                else:\\\\n                    # These trials go to training set\\\\n                    for trial_idx in trials_in_set:\\\\n                        train_neural[session].append(neural[session][trial_idx])\\\\n                        train_input[session].append(input[session][trial_idx])\\\\n                        train_output[session].append(output[session][trial_idx])\\\\n\\\\n        # Train decoder on training data\\\\n        model = train_decoder(train_neural, train_input, train_output, metadata={}, **kwargs)\\\\n\\\\n        # Predict on test data\\\\n        test_predictions, test_pc, confidences = predict(test_neural, test_input, model)\\\\n\\\\n        # Store predictions in the correct positions\\\\n        for session in range(nsessions):\\\\n            for idx, trial_idx in enumerate(test_trial_indices[session]):\\\\n                all_predictions[session][trial_idx] = test_predictions[session][idx]\\\\n                all_pcs[session][trial_idx] = test_pc[session][idx]\\\\n                all_confidences[session][trial_idx] = confidences[session][idx]\\\\n\\\\n    # Compute evaluation metric across all sessions and trials\\\\n    scores = eval_fn(all_predictions, output)\\\\n\\\\n    return scores, all_predictions, all_pcs, all_confidences, trial_splits\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef train_validate_decoder(neural: list, input: list, output: list, metadata: str | None = None,\\\\n                            frac_train: float = 0.8,\\\\n                            eval_fn=None, state=None,\\\\n                            **kwargs):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    Validates the decoder by training on frac_train of trials and testing on the rest.\\\\n    Every session has some trials in training and some in test.\\\\n\\\\n    Inputs:\\\\n        neural: neural activity. neural is a list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list\\\\n                of length ntrials[session], and neural[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (nneurons[session], T[session][trial]),\\\\n                dtype = float32, giving the neural activity for that trial\\\\n        input: variables beyond neural activity the decoder should input, e.g. the stimulis, condition. input is a list of\\\\n                length nsessions, input[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and input[session][trial] is a numpy array of\\\\n                shape (dinput, T[session][trial]), dtype = float32. with the input variable(s) for each timepoint.\\\\n                dinput is the number of inputs. for session in range(nsessions):\\\\n        for idx, trial_idx in enumerate(train_indices[session]):\\\\n            all_predictions[session][trial_idx] = train_predictions[session][idx]\\\\n _train_decoder_pca_logistic(neural: list, input: list, output: list, metadata: dict = {}, **kwargs):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    Trains a common decoder for all sessions to predict output from neural and input data.\\\\n    Concatenates data across trials for each session, then projects the neural data for each session onto its first npcs principal components.\\\\n    Then, concatenates data across all sessions and trains a common decoder across all sessions using logistic regression to predict output from the\\\\n    projected neural data and input data.\\\\n\\\\n dict = {}, **kwargs):\\n   694→    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n   695→    Trains a common decoder for all sessions to predict output from neural and input data.\\n   696→    Jointly learns projection matrices for each session and separate shared decoders for each output dimension.\\n   697→\\n   698→    Inputs:\\n   699→        neural: neural activity. neural is a list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list\\n   700→                of length ntrials[session], and neural[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (nneurons[session], T[session][trial]),\\n   701→                dtype = float32, giving the neural activity for that trial\\n   702→        input: variables beyond neural activity the decoder should input, e.g. the stimulis, condition. input is a list of\\n   703→                length nsessions, input[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and input[session][trial] is a numpy array of\\n   704→                shape (dinput, T[session][trial]), dtype = float32. with the input variable(s) for each timepoint.\\n   705→                dinput is the number of inputs. For discrete inputs, use a one-hot encoding.\\n   706→        output: variables we want to decode. output is a list of length nsessions, output[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],\\n   707→                and output[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]) of dtype = int with\\n   708→                categorical values for each timepoint. Each output[idx, t] is an integer from 0 to ncategories[idx]-1.\\n   709→        metadata: optional dict with additional information about the experiment.\\n   710→\\n   711→        Algorithm hyperparameters can be passed as keyword arguments:\\n   712→        npcs: number of projected dimensions to use (default: 10)\\n   713→        num_epochs: number of training epochs (default: 200)\\n   714→        lr: learning rate (default: 0.001)\\n   715→        l1_weight: L1 regularization weight for projection matrices (default: 1e-4)\\n   716→        svd_max_samples: maximum number of timepoints to use for SVD initialization (default: 50000).\\n   717→                         If a session has more timepoints than this, a random subset will be used.\\n   718→        svd_max_neurons: maximum number of neurons to use for SVD initialization (default: 2000).\\n   719→                         If a session has more neurons than this, random Gaussian projection will be used.\\n   720→                         The final weight is the product of the random projection and SVD matrices.\\n   721→        ncategories: optional list of length doutput giving number of categories for each output dimension.\\n   722→                     If not provided, will be inferred from data.\\n   723→        balanced_loss: if True, use class-weighted cross-entropy loss to compensate for class imbalance.\\n   724→                       Weights are inverse of class frequency. Default: False.\\n   725→\\n   726→    Returns:\\n   727→        model: dict with trained decoder parameters. dict with the keys:\\n   728→            'projection': list of length nsessions, projection[session] is a torch tensor of shape (npcs, nneurons[session])\\n   729→            'decoder': list of length doutput, decoder[out_dim] is a torch linear layer for that output dimension\\n   730→            'ncategories': list of length doutput, ncategories[out_dim] is the number of categories for that output\\n   731→            'device': torch device used for training\\n   732→\\n   733→    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n   734→\\n   735→    model = {\\n   736→        'projection': [],\\n   737→        'decoder': [],\\n   738→        'ncategories': [],\\n   739→        'device': None\\n   740→    }\\n   741→\\n   742→    npcs = kwargs.get('npcs', 10)\\n   743→    num_epochs = kwargs.get('num_epochs', 200)\\n   744→    lr = kwargs.get('lr', 0.001)\\n   745→    l1_weight = kwargs.get('l1_weight', 1e-4)\\n   746→    device_str = kwargs.get('device', None)\\n   747→    balanced_loss = kwargs.get('balanced_loss', False)\\n   748→\\n   749→    nsessions = len(neural)\\n   750→    if device_str is not None:\\n   751→        device = torch.device(device_str)\\n   752→    else:\\n   753→        device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')\\n   754→\\n   755→    model['device'] = device\\n   756→    print('Using device:', device)\\n   757→\\n   758→    # Prepare training data using helper function\\n   759→    session_data, dinput, doutput = _prepare_session_data(neural, input, output, device)\\n   760→\\n   761→    # Determine number of categories for each output dimension\\n   762→    if 'ncategories' in kwargs:\\n   763→        ncategories = kwargs['ncategories']\\n   764→    else:\\n   765→        ncategories = []\\n   766→        for out_dim in range(doutput):\\n   767→            max_cat = 0\\n   768→            for session in range(nsessions):\\n   769→                if session_data[session] is None:\\n   770→                    continue\\n   771→                max_cat = max(max_cat, int(session_data[session]['output'][:, out_dim].max().item()))\\n   772→            ncategories.append(max_cat + 1)\\n   773→\\n   774→    model['ncategories'] = ncategories\\n   775→\\n   776→    # Compute class weights (always, for use in chance computation and optionally for balanced loss)\\n   777→    class_weights = []\\n   778→    class_fractions = []  # Store fractions for chance computation\\n   779→    for out_dim in range(doutput):\\n   780→        # Count occurrences of each class across all sessions\\n   781→        class_counts = np.zeros(ncategories[out_dim])\\n   782→        for session in range(nsessions):\\n   783→            if session_data[session] is None:\\n   784→                continue\\n   785→            outputs = session_data[session]['output'][:, out_dim].cpu().numpy()\\n   786→            for c in range(ncategories[out_dim]):\\n   787→                class_counts[c] += np.sum(outputs == c)\\n   788→        # Store class fractions for chance computation\\n   789→        total = np.sum(class_counts)\\n   790→        fractions = class_counts / total\\n   791→        class_fractions.append(fractions)\\n   792→        # Compute weights as inverse of frequency (with smoothing to avoid division by zero)\\n   793→        weights = total / (ncategories[out_dim] * np.maximum(class_counts, 1))\\n   794→        # Normalize weights to sum to 1 (so each output dimension is equally weighted)\\n   795→        weights = weights / np.sum(weights)\\n   796→        class_weights.append(torch.tensor(weights, dtype=torch.float32, device=device))\\n   797→\\n   798→    model['class_weights'] = class_weights\\n   799→    model['class_fractions'] = class_fractions\\n   800→\\n   801→    if balanced_loss:\\n   802→        print(f\\\"Using balanced loss with class weights:\\\")\\n   803→        for out_dim in range(doutput):\\n   804→            print(f\\\"  Output {out_dim}: {class_weights[out_dim].cpu().numpy()}\\\")\\n   805→\\n   806→    # Initialize projection matrices for each session\\n   807→    svd_max_samples = kwargs.get('svd_max_samples', 50000)  # Max timepoints to use for SVD initialization\\n   808→    svd_max_neurons = kwargs.get('svd_max_neurons', 2000)   # Max neurons to use for SVD initialization\\n   809→    projection_layers = []\\n   810→    for session in range(nsessions):\\n   811→        nneurons = session_data[session]['nneurons']\\n   812→        proj = nn.Linear(nneurons, npcs, bias=False).to(device)\\n   813→\\n   814→        # Initialize with SVD for stability (use V from SVD of neural data)\\n   815→        # For neural data with shape (n_timepoints, n_neurons), SVD gives principal components in V\\n   816→        # Use random subsets if data is too large\\n   817→        n_timepoints = session_data[session]['neural'].shape[0]\\n   818→\\n   819→        # Sample timepoints if needed\\n   820→        if n_timepoints > svd_max_samples:\\n   821→            time_indices = torch.randperm(n_timepoints)[:svd_max_samples]\\n   822→            neural_subset = session_data[session]['neural'][time_indices, :]\\n   823→            print(f\\\"Session {session}: Using {svd_max_samples} of {n_timepoints} timepoints for SVD initialization\\\")\\n   824→        else:\\n   825→            neural_subset = session_data[session]['neural']\\n   826→\\n   827→        # Use random projection if too many neurons\\n   828→        if nneurons > svd_max_neurons:\\n   829→            # Create random Gaussian projection matrix: (n_neurons, svd_max_neurons)\\n   830→            P = torch.randn(nneurons, svd_max_neurons)\\n   831→            # Project neural data: (n_timepoints, n_neurons) @ (n_neurons, svd_max_neurons) = (n_timepoints, svd_max_neurons)\\n   832→            neural_projected = neural_subset @ P\\n   833→            print(f\\\"Session {session}: Using random projection to {svd_max_neurons} of {nneurons} neurons for SVD initialization\\\")\\n   834→\\n   835→            # SVD on projected data\\n   836→            _, _, V = torch.svd(neural_projected, some=True)\\n   837→            # V has shape (svd_max_neurons, min(n_timepoints_subset, svd_max_neurons))\\n   838→\\n   839→            # Compose: final weight = (P @ V[:, :npcs]).T = V[:, :npcs].T @ P.T\\n   840→            n_components = min(npcs, V.shape[1])\\n   841→            proj.weight.data[:n_components, :] = (V[:, :n_components].T @ P.T).to(device).clone()\\n   842→        else:\\n   843→            # Standard SVD without random projection\\n   844→            _, _, V = torch.svd(neural_subset, some=True)\\n   845→            # V has shape (n_neurons, min(n_timepoints_subset, n_neurons))\\n   846→            n_components = min(npcs, V.shape[1])\\n   847→            proj.weight.data[:n_components, :] = V[:, :n_components].T.to(device).clone()\\n   848→\\n   849→        # Initialize remaining components randomly if needed\\n   850→        if n_components < npcs:\\n   851→            nn.init.orthogonal_(proj.weight.data[n_components:, :])\\n   852→\\n   853→        projection_layers.append(proj)\\n   854→\\n   855→    # Initialize separate decoders for each output dimension\\n   856→    decoders = []\\n   857→    for out_dim in range(doutput):\\n   858→        decoder = nn.Linear(npcs + dinput, ncategories[out_dim]).to(device)\\n   859→        decoders.append(decoder)\\n   860→\\n   861→    # Collect all parameters\\n   862→    all_params = []\\n   863→    for proj in projection_layers:\\n   864→        all_params.extend(proj.parameters())\\n   865→    for decoder in decoders:\\n   866→        all_params.extend(decoder.parameters())\\n   867→\\n   868→    optimizer = optim.Adam(all_params, lr=lr)\\n   869→\\n   870→    # Loss function with reduction='none' for manual weighting (matches torch_brain)\\n   871→    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction='none')\\n   872→\\n   873→    # Training loop\\n   874→    # Data stays on CPU; each session is moved to GPU one at a time.\\n   875→    # backward() is called per session to free the computation graph before\\n   876→    # loading the next session. Gradients accumulate across sessions.\\n   877→    for epoch in range(num_epochs):\\n   878→        epoch_loss = 0.\\n   879→        optimizer.zero_grad()\\n   880→\\n   881→        for session in range(nsessions):\\n   882→            if session_data[session] is None:\\n   883→                continue\\n   884→            # Move this session's data to device\\n   885→            neural_batch = session_data[session]['neural'].to(device)\\n   886→            input_batch = session_data[session]['input'].to(device)\\n   887→            output_batch = session_data[session]['output'].to(device)\\n   888→\\n   889→            # Forward pass - shared projection\\n   890→            projected = projection_layers[session](neural_batch)\\n   891→            combined = torch.cat([projected, input_batch], dim=1)\\n   892→\\n   893→            # Compute loss for each output dimension\\n   894→            session_loss = torch.tensor(0., device=device)\\n   895→            for out_dim in range(doutput):\\n   896→                logits = decoders[out_dim](combined)\\n   897→                target = output_batch[:, out_dim]\\n   898→                loss_per_sample = criterion(logits, target)\\n   899→\\n   900→                if balanced_loss:\\n   901→                    # Manual per-sample weighting (matches torch_brain exactly)\\n   902→                    sample_weights = class_weights[out_dim][target]\\n   903→                    session_loss += (sample_weights * loss_per_sample).sum() / sample_weights.sum()\\n   904→                else:\\n   905→                    session_loss += loss_per_sample.mean()\\n   906→\\n   907→            # Add L1 regularization on current session's projection matrix\\n   908→            if l1_weight > 0:\\n   909→                l1_loss = torch.sum(torch.abs(projection_layers[session].weight))\\n   910→                session_loss += l1_weight * l1_loss\\n   911→\\n   912→            # Backward per session: frees computation graph, accumulates gradients\\n   913→            session_loss.backward()\\n   914→            epoch_loss += session_loss.item()\\n   915→\\n   916→        optimizer.step()\\n   917→\\n   918→        if ((epoch + 1) % 10 == 0) or (epoch < 10):\\n   919→            # Loss is sum of per-output-dim means across sessions\\n   920→            # Normalize by (nsessions * doutput) to get average per output per session\\n   921→            train_loss_normalized = epoch_loss / (nsessions * doutput)\\n   922→            print(f'Epoch [{epoch+1}/{num_epochs}], Loss: {train_loss_normalized:.6f}')\\n   923→\\n   924→    # Store trained parameters\\n   925→    for session in range(nsessions):\\n   926→        model['projection'].append(projection_layers[session].weight.data.clone())\\n   927→    model['decoder'] = decoders\\n   928→\\n   929→    return model\\n   930→\\n   931→def predict(neural: list, input: list, model: dict, sessionid: list | None = None, metadata: dict = {}):\\n   932→    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n   933→    Uses a trained decoder model to predict output from neural and input data.\\n   934→\\n   935→    Inputs:\\n   936→        neural: neural activity. neural is a list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list\\n   937→                of length ntrials[session], and neural[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (nneurons[session], T[session][trial]),\\n   938→                dtype = float32, giving the neural activity for that trial\\n   939→        input: variables beyond neural activity the decoder should input, e.g. the stimulis, condition. input is a list of\\n   940→                length nsessions, input[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and input[session][trial] is a numpy array of\\n   941→                shape (dinput, T[session][trial]), dtype = float32. with the input variable(s) for each timepoint.\\n   942→                dinput is the number of inputs. For discrete inputs, use a one-hot encoding.\\n   943→        model: dict with trained decoder parameters. dict with the keys:\\n   944→                'projection': list of length nsessions, 'ncategories': list of length doutput with number of categories per output dimension\\n   947→                'device': torch device\\n   948→        sessionid: optional list of length nsessions, giving the IDs of the sessions.\\n   949→        metadata: optional dict with additional information about the experiment.\\n   950→    Returns:\\n   951→        predictions: list of length nsessions,           with the predicted categorical output variable(s) for each timepoint.\\n   954→        pcs: list of length nsessions, pcs[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],\\n   955→                and pcs[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (npcs, T[session][trial]) with the projected neural data.\\n   956→        confidences: list of length nsessions, confidences[session] is a list of 959→\\n   960→    nsessions = len(neural)\\n   961→    device = model['device']\\n   962→    decoders = model['decoder']\\n   963→    doutput = len(decoders)\\n   964→\\n   965→    # Replicate 1D data instead of original\\n   981→    input = input_processed\\n   982→\\n   983→    confidences = []\\n   984→    predictions = []\\n   985→    pcs = []\\n   986→\\n   987→    with torch.no_grad():\\n   988→        for sessionidx in range(nsessions):\\n   989→            if sessionid is not None:\\n   990→                session = sessionid[sessionidx]\\n   991→            else:\\n   992→                session = sessionidx\\n   993→\\n   994→            ntrials = len(neural[sessionidx])\\n   995→            session_predictions = []\\n   996→            session_confidences = []\\n   997→            session_pcs = []\\n   998→            projection = model['projection'][session]\\n   999→\\n  1000→            for trial in range(ntrials):\\n  1001→ torch.from_numpy(input[sessionidx][trial].T.astype(np.float32)).to(device)    # (T, dinput)\\n  1004→\\n  1005→                # Project neural data\\n  1006→                projected = torch.matmul(neural_trial, projection.T)  # (T, npcs)\\n  1007→\\n  1008→                # Decode each output dimension\\n  1009→                combined = torch.cat([projected, input_trial], dim=1)                  pred[:, out_dim] = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1).cpu().numpy()\\n  1016→                    prob = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)\\n  1017→                    conf[:, out_dim] = session_confidences.append(conf.T)  # (doutput, T)\\n  1022→                session_pcs.append(projected.cpu().numpy().T)  # (npcs, T)\\n  1023→\\n  1024→            predictions.append(session_predictions)\\n  1025→            pcs.append(session_pcs)\\n  1026→            confidences.append(session_confidences)\\n  1027→\\n  1028→    return predictions, pcs, confidences\\n  1029→\\n  1030→def f1scores_all_sessions(all_predictions: list, output: list):\\n  1031→    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n  1032→    Concatenate all predictions and ground truth to compute F1 scores  1041→        f1scores: numpy array of shape (doutput,) with the F1 score for each output dimension\\n  1042→    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n  1043→    nsessions = len(all_predictions)\\n  1044→    all_pred_concat     output_trial_expanded = np.tile(output_trial[:, np.newaxis], (1, T)).T  # (T, doutput)\\n  1060→                all_output_concat.append(output_trial_expanded)\\n  1061→            else:\\n  1062→ 1068→\\n  1069→    # Compute F1 score for each output dimension (macro average for multiclass)\\n  1070→    f1scores = np.zeros(doutput)\\n  1071→    for out_dim in range(doutput):\\n  1072→        f1scores[out_dim] = f1_score(all_output_concat[:, out_dim], all_pred_concat[:, out_dim], average='macro')\\n  1073→\\n  1074→    return f1scores\\n  1075→\\n  1076→def Files and Code Sections:\\n   - `/app/methods.txt` - Paper methods describing task paradigm, videography, electrophysiology, behavioral analysis\\n   - `/app/code/WorkingWithDataObjs.m` - Tutorial on data structure; key params: alignEvent='goCue', dt=1/100, tmin=-2.5, tmax=2.5, smooth=15, bctype='reflect', quality='all', lowFR=1\\n   - `/app/code/DataLoadingScripts/processData.m` - Processing pipeline: findTrials → findClusters → alignSpikes → getSeq → removeLowFRClusters → baselineFR\\n   - `/app/code/DataLoadingScripts/getSeq.m` - Spike binning and smoothing: `N = histc(trialtm_aligned, edges)`, `trialdat = mySmooth(N./params.dt, params.smooth, params.bctype)`\\n   - `/app/code/DataLoadingScripts/alignSpikes.m` - `trialtm_aligned = trialtm - goCue(trial)`\\n   - `/app/code/DataLoadingScripts/findClusters.m` - Quality filter excluding 'garbage', 'gabrga', 'noisy', 'real?'\\n   - `/app/code/DataLoadingScripts/removeLowFRClusters.m` - `meanFRs = mean(mean(psth,3),1); use = meanFRs > lowFR`\\n   - `/app/code/utils/mySmooth.m` - Causal Gaussian: `kern = gausswin(N); kern(1:floor(N/2)) = 0; kern = kern./sum(kern)`, with 'reflect' boundary: `x_filt = cat(1, x(1:N,:), x)`\\n   - `/app/code/DataLoadingScripts/loadMotionEnergy.m` - ME alignment: `interp1(frameTimes-vidshift-alignTimes(trix), me.data{trix}, taxis)`\\n   - `/app/code/funcs/findVideoOffset.m` - `vidshift = mode(sglx.bitcode.bitstart)/sglx.fs - mode(bp.ev.bitStart)`\\n   - `/app/code/DataLoadingScripts/Recording and video/loadJEB15_ALMVideo.m` - Contains comment \\\"excluding first three sessions, they look like they were in a more sensory area\\\" but sessions are NOT commented out\\n   - `/app/train_decoder.py` - Decoder training script; uses train_validate_decoder with 80/20 split\\n   - `/app/decoder.py` - Full decoder implementation including verify_data_format, train_decoder, predict, accuracy functions\\n   \\n   - `/app/convert_data.py` (CREATED) - Main conversion script. Key sections:\\n     - Session definitions: 44 sessions (25 Ephys + 19 RandomizedDelay) from 14 mice with probe assignments\\n     - `gausswin()`: MATLAB-equivalent Gaussian window\\n     - `causal_smooth()`: Causal Gaussian smoothing matching mySmooth.m\\n     - `compute_speed()`: Speed from (x,y) with NaN filling for missing DLC positions\\n     - `fill_positions_nearest()`: Fill invalid positions with nearest valid values\\n     - `process_session()`: Processes one session - loads HDF5, bins spikes, smooths, filters neurons, computes DLC velocities, loads motion energy\\n     - `convert_all()`: Iterates sessions, assembles final data dict, saves pickle\\n     - CLI args: `--output` (path), `--sample` (N sessions to process)\\n\\n   - `/app/sample_data.pkl` (CREATED) - 3-session sample dataset (EKH1, EKH3, JEB6), 796 trials, 143 neurons total\\n\\n4. Errors and Fixes:\\n   - **Tongue velocity all \\\"high\\\" (1.0)**: Root cause: tongue DLC positions are NaN for ~96% of frames (tongue not visible). After filling NaN with nearest valid position, velocity is 0 during non-visible periods. The 50th percentile = 0, so all values >= 0 are classified as \\\"high\\\".\\n     - Fix attempt 1: Changed `fill_missing=False` to `fill_missing=True` in compute_speed for tongue - still all 1s because filled positions are constant (velocity stays 0)\\n     - Fix attempt 2 (SUCCESSFUL): Compute 50th percentile on NON-ZERO values only for tongue velocity. Zero values (tongue not visible) automatically become \\\"low\\\". Result: ~93% low, ~7% high per session.\\n   \\n   - **EKH3 quality label '\\\\x00\\\\x00'**: One cluster had null bytes as quality label. Handled by the filter that excludes empty strings (`q != ''`).\\n\\n   - **HDF5 structure complexity**: MATLAB cell arrays are stored as arrays of HDF5 object references. Required careful dereferencing with `f[ref][()]` patterns. Feature names required double dereferencing (cell array of cell array of strings).\\n\\n5.
